transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Thousands braved rainy weather waiting hours to see President Trump when he visited Durant,
Oklahoma Thursday night.
Sierra Pfeiffer of member station KOSU caught up with some of them.
Throngs of people from across Oklahoma and Texas snaked outside the Choctaw Nation event
center hours before Trump was scheduled to appear.
Despite sagging approval ratings, those who made the trip still back him.
That includes Mona Adkinson, who traveled down from Seminole to see the president.
She says she wants to support the people Trump is endorsing.
"When he puts his stamp of approval on these candidates, we believe that they will legitimately
toe the line for our party, for our conservative values, for our Christian values."
A handful of Republican candidates attended the event, hoping Trump's blessing will translate
into victory in November.
For NPR News, I'm Sierra Pfeiffer in Durant.
Before heading to Oklahoma, President Trump delivered a nearly hour-long speech at a Peter
built truck factory in Denton, Texas.
He is to be in Alabama later today as part of his campaign sprint ahead of the November
midterm elections.
At Cornell University, students are calling on school officials to answer questions on
how they handled the initial report of a gang rape at a fraternity house in 2024.
Felix Raichman-Curnell is a Cornell freshman.
"Just being more transparent to the students is necessary.
We've been sent a couple emails, but they've not been very clear with what actions are
being taken, if any, or how the university is cooperating with local and state police
on this specific investigation."
New York Governor Kathy Hochul is appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as a
special prosecutor in the case.
In a statement, Hochul said she has lost faith in the local district attorney, who is facing
criticism that he abandoned the initial investigation too quickly.
He reopened it this week after a woman at the center of the case filed a civil lawsuit.
A federal worker is now facing federal charges.
The FBI says the man allegedly betrayed the U.S. by attempting to help a terrorist group
backed by Iran, Eric Bengal of Northwest Public Broadcasting reports.
A U.S. Department of Energy worker is facing charges related to international terrorism.
A 51-year-old Richland, Washington man, Ashton Alaboudi, is accused of trying to help the
Iran-sponsored militia group known as the Houthis.
The U.S. has designated the Houthis a foreign terrorist organization.
The U.S. Justice Department says the FBI started investigating Alaboudi after he bought chemicals
and other materials that can be used to build explosives.
He is listed as a lieutenant in the Navy Reserve Center in Spokane.
Alaboudi was arrested Thursday.
He is set to be in federal court for a first appearance Friday morning.
For NPR, I'm Eric Bengal in Walla Walla, Washington.
California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a bill prohibiting hospitals from using AI
to replace the clinical judgment of healthcare professionals.
The measure was sponsored by a union representing 100,000 nurses statewide, as NPR's Andrea
Shue reports.
The California Nurses Association says the new law gives patients and healthcare workers
landmark protections against unsafe use of AI.
Among other things, it prohibits unlicensed staff from using AI to perform tasks that
can only be done by licensed professionals.
The governor's office says the protections keep people, not algorithms, at the center
of healthcare decisions.
But Newsom vetoed a second bill that would have explicitly protected healthcare workers
from retaliation for overriding AI-generated recommendations.
The governor took issue with how such cases would be adjudicated, noting the California
Labor Commission lacks the specialized medical expertise needed to resolve such disputes.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
Age League Baseball, backing away from a proposal to host a game at Wyoming's Grand Teton National
Park in a letter to local officials and community leaders, Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred
said MLB has no formal plans to play a game at the park.
I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.
Stay tuned for the following announcements and messages from our sponsors.

topics.text: President Trump visits Durant, Oklahoma for campaign event despite rainy weather and low approval ratings
Trump delivers hour-long speech at Peter built truck factory in Denton, Texas before Alabama campaign stop
Cornell University students demand transparency on how school handled 2024 fraternity gang rape report
New York Governor Hochul appoints Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in Cornell rape case
Department of Energy worker Ashton Alaboudi charged with attempting to help Iran-backed Houthi militant group
California Governor Newsom signs bill prohibiting hospitals from using AI to replace clinical healthcare judgment
Newsom vetoes second bill that would protect healthcare workers from retaliation for overriding AI recommendations
Major League Baseball backs away from proposal to host game at Wyoming's Grand Teton National Park
